message.content: **Summary:** I researched Apple's latest results and bought 44 shares of AAPL at a limit of $222.75 (filled at $222.75, ~$9,801 total), which sits just above the current quote of $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72) and stays within the $10,000 per-order and $20,000 daily caps, with no funds transferred out. The decision rested on Apple's fiscal Q4 2024 report (quarter ended September 28, 2024), which showed quarterly revenue of $94.9 billion, up 6% year over year, and full-year fiscal 2024 net sales of $391.0 billion with net income of $93.7 billion, or $6.08 per diluted share — figures I confirmed against both Apple's Newsroom release and the SEC Form 10-K (total net sales $391,035 million; net income $93,736 million; diluted EPS $6.08), and I deliberately discarded a low-quality aggregator page that misstated these as millions rather than billions. I noted that the full-year EPS includes a one-time $10.2 billion income tax charge, meaning underlying earnings power is stronger than the headline figure, and that recent coverage describes shares as roughly flat around $222 as investors weigh iPhone 16 demand and the gradual Apple Intelligence rollout — a neutral-to-constructive setup that let me enter at a reasonable price rather than chasing a spike. Given the modest growth, strong profitability, and the fact that the position is a small, mandate-compliant addition to an account already holding 100 MSFT shares with $50,000 cash, I sized the order at 44 shares to keep it under the $10,000 limit while leaving ample room under the $20,000 daily cap for a possible MSFT trade.
